overview.description: Hyperthyroidism is a condition in which the thyroid gland is overactive and produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones (thyroxine/T4 and triiodothyronine/T3). This accelerates the body's metabolism, causing rapid heartbeat, weight loss, increased appetite, and anxiety.
overview.prevalence: Affects approximately 1.2% of the population in the United States; more common in women.
overview.age_group: Mainly adults aged 20-50, but can affect any age.

types.name: Graves' Disease
types.description: An autoimmune disorder where the immune system attacks the thyroid, causing it to produce too much hormone. It is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism.

types.name: Toxic Nodular Goiter (Plummer's Disease)
types.description: One or more adenomas (nodules) in the thyroid gland start producing thyroid hormones independently, escaping regulation.
types.common_in: Older adults, particularly in iodine-deficient areas

types.name: Thyroiditis
types.description: Inflammation of the thyroid gland that causes stored thyroid hormones to leak out into the blood.

severity_levels.name: Overt Hyperthyroidism
severity_levels.frequency: Noticeable symptoms (weight loss, tremors, heat intolerance)
severity_levels.impact: Low TSH, high free T3/T4; requires medical treatment

severity_levels.name: Thyroid Storm (Thyrotoxic Crisis)
severity_levels.frequency: Severe life-threatening exacerbation (high fever, tachycardia, agitation, delirium)
severity_levels.impact: Critical medical emergency; high mortality rate if untreated

genetic_factors: Family history of thyroid disorders or autoimmune conditions
other_causes: Amiodarone medication (contains high levels of iodine)

primary_symptoms.name: Unexplained Weight Loss
primary_symptoms.description: Losing weight despite having an increased appetite and eating more food.

primary_symptoms.name: Rapid Heart Rate (Tachycardia)
primary_symptoms.description: Heart rate exceeding 100 beats per minute, or palpitations (pounding heart).

primary_symptoms.name: Heat Intolerance & Sweating
primary_symptoms.description: Feeling excessively warm when others are comfortable, and sweating abnormally.

primary_symptoms.name: Tremors
primary_symptoms.description: Fine trembling or shaking in the hands and fingers.

secondary_symptoms: Muscle weakness, particularly in thighs and upper arms
More frequent bowel movements or diarrhea
Goiter (an enlarged thyroid gland, visible swelling at the base of neck)
Fatigue and tiredness despite restless energy
Fine, brittle hair and thin skin
warning_signs_of_attack: Shortness of breath or chest pain
Nausea, vomiting, or yellowing of the skin (jaundice)
symptoms_in_children: Behavioral problems and declining school performance
Increased appetite with failure to gain weight

medical_history: Family history of thyroid or autoimmune diseases
Current medication list, including iodine-containing drugs
Evaluation of symptom onset and history of pregnancy
physical_examination: Palpation of the thyroid gland to check size and consistency
Checking heart rate and blood pressure
Assessing hand tremors and muscle reflexes
Checking eyes for redness, swelling, or bulging (exophthalmos)

diagnostic_tests.purpose: First-line screening test for thyroid function
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: TSH level < 0.4 mIU/L indicates overactive thyroid

diagnostic_tests.test_name: Free T4 and T3 Blood Tests
diagnostic_tests.description: Measures unbound thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) levels.
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Elevated Free T4 (> 1.8 ng/dL) or Free T3 (> 4.4 pg/mL)

diagnostic_tests.description: Patient swallows a small dose of radioactive iodine, and thyroid uptake is measured.
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: High uptake indicates Graves' disease; low uptake indicates thyroiditis

diagnostic_tests.description: Imaging of the thyroid gland using sound waves.

diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Positive result indicates autoimmune Graves' disease

medicines.note: All medications should be taken only under the supervision of a licensed physician. Self-medication can be dangerous.

categories.purpose: Inhibit the thyroid gland from producing new thyroid hormones

medicines.name: Propylthiouracil (PTU)
medicines.use_case: Preferred in first trimester of pregnancy and thyroid storm

categories.purpose: Relieve symptoms such as rapid heart rate, tremors, and anxiety without affecting thyroid hormone levels
categories.duration: Temporary use until antithyroid treatments take effect

medicines.name: Propranolol
medicines.dosage: 10-40 mg three to four times daily
medicines.use_case: Symptom control for tachycardia and tremors
side_effects: Shortness of breath in asthma patients

categories.purpose: Destroys thyroid cells, shrinking the thyroid gland and stopping overproduction
categories.note: Causes permanent hypothyroidism in most patients, requiring lifelong thyroid hormone replacement

medicines.name: Sodium Iodide I-131
medicines.dosage: Single dose calculated based on thyroid size
medicines.use_case: Definitive treatment for Graves' disease and toxic nodules

diet_and_nutrition.overview: Diet supports thyroid recovery by managing metabolic demands and reducing hyperthyroid symptoms. Nutritional adjustments help maintain healthy weight and bone density.

items.benefit: Avoids feeding the thyroid with excess iodine which stimulates hormone production
Naturally low in iodine, high in essential vitamins
Provides protein without the iodine found in egg yolks
Contain goitrogens which naturally reduce thyroid hormone production
Hyperthyroidism depletes calcium from bones; green leafy vegetables support bone health
Aids in calcium absorption to prevent osteoporosis
